_doc: The percussion rack AS IT STANDS — read back from the running Reaper rack through tools/aro_state.js (2026-09-18, after his 'done loading'; RUNNING_LOG §39). One row per track: the channel it filters on `port`, the Spitfire (C) preset it holds, the articulation he selected inside it (index = the preset's keyswitch order), the banked state that reproduces the preset as text (bank/aro_states/), and the catalog entry that names its keys (`catalogStatus` says how far that map can be trusted; `keysFrom` says which preset form the catalog's map was dictated from, where known). This file is the INPUT to the key sweep and, once keys are confirmed, to bank/perc_selection.json. It is a record, not a control: the tracks are made by reaper/bridge/jobs/make_perc_tracks.lua.

tracks.artic: Crashers and Stack - All in One

tracks.note: HIS CHOICE 2026-09-18 ("yes alt bass instead I believe it has an extra mallet or articulation"): the measured ch-12 track is his own Bass Drum Alt ARO, not Bass Drum ARO. Both filter on LGPerc ch 12, so only one can be recorded (RUNNING_LOG §49–§50) and the probe schedule is unchanged in port and channel. READ from the running rack: preset "Bass Drum (Alt) (C)", 7 articulations (Sticks · Hard Felt Undamped · Hard Felt Damped · Medium · Brushes · Rods · All-in-one), All-in-one selected — SIX beaters where the main Bass Drum (GC) has seven, which is the extra articulation he remembered. The catalog link therefore changed to bass_drum_alt, whose map genuinely differs (key 41 is Rim Hit L there, Single Hit L on bass_drum). State banked 2026-09-18.

_trimsNote: PLAN 1b.3, 2026-09-19 (RUNNING_LOG §83): trims recomputed to an ABSOLUTE target — a 9-voice tutti at -20 LUFS-S, so each voice at -31.84 dB on the instrument card’s scale. 0d’s figures were relative and were measured through a REC bus 12 dB down; every one of these is a CUT. Percussion is judged on the loudest 400 ms (0d’s rule — a one-shot’s integrated level follows its ring). Source: bank/trims.json.
